name: UH MANOA LANAI FREE CULTURAL EVENT - MONKEY WATERFALL DANCE TROUPE
venue: Four Seasons Resorts Lanai, The Lodge at Koele
description: A premier Hawaiian dance troupe, dear to many hearts here on Lanai. If you visit their web site at http://www.monkeywaterfall.org/New_MWF/Home.html, you’ll immediately recognize the two dancers who entertained us in the Great Hall in the final year of the Art & Story project; they performed a dance based on a traditional Chinese fable that featured a little red monkey and 10-foot tall man who danced the entire performance on stilts, both in stunning masks. The tiny, graceful dancer in the red velvet monkey suit was Monkey Waterfall’s principal, Yukie Shiroma, who was the dance movement coach for all 5 years of Art & Story. Yukie inspired over 100 young Lanai students and you will see why and be inspired yourselves when you see this show. Celebrating their 20th anniversary, Monkey Waterfall returns to Lanai bringing a full-evening of dance, theatre, storytelling, masks, and puppets. The program includes their signature piece and some old and new work.

name: LOVE2
description:
Written and Directed by Siobhan Ni Dhonacha

We all hurt people, and we are all hurt people. This is the story of four couples, in varying stages of coupling and uncoupling, and their life choices, choices that most of us face every day. Tell a white lie, hide our true feelings, believe in love, run away, remain loyal, have faith, dig deep, give up. What would we do? And what do we do when faced with these moments of decision?

name: MAIZOME
description:
At the “Maizome” academy students of all ages will perform various dances and shamisen numbers in a showcase of what they learned last year.  The “Maizome” has been an annual tradition for the Hanayagi Dancing Academy since Hanayagi Mitsuaki founded the organization in 1947. The academy was established on the guiding principle of preserving and perpetuating the classical performing arts of Japan. The academy later incorporated as the Hanayagi Dancing Academy Foundation Hawaii in 2004.

Mission Memorial Auditorium is one of three distinctive red-brick buildings located on the Frank F. Fasi Civic Center grounds. The structures were built in 1916 as a tribute to the American Protestant mission to Hawaii. No food or drinks will be allowed in the auditorium.

550 South King Street, next to Honolulu Hale

name: THE HOLIDAY OF RAIN
description:
At the Sadie Thompson Inn in Samoa, the innkeepers have planned an unusual experience for their special guests: a reenactment of W. Somerset Maugham’s 1921 short story “Rain.” But thanks to a magician’s time warp, the real Maugham finds himself on the guest list. Swirling together fantasy, history, humor and drama, Victoria Nalani Kneubuhl, winner of the Hawaii Award for Literature and the author of The Conversion of Kaahumanu and Ola Na Iwi, re-imagines Maugham’s steamy South Sea story in a wild romp of illusions, delusions and near fatal attractions.

Tickets are on sale now and prices range from $5 to $20.  Tickets may be purchased with a credit card by calling 536-4441, or by visiting the Kumu Kahua Box Office at 46 Merchant Street from 11am to 3pm Monday through Friday.  For more information about this and other productions, or to purchase tickets online, visit www. Kumu Kahua.org.

name: PRINCE KUHIO CELEBRATION - HULA KAHIKO
venue: Grand Hyatt Kauai Resort and Spa
description: As part of the Prince Kuhio Celebration, come learn the story of ancient hula (hula kahiko), hula chants and find out about kinolau (plants) as they relate to hula kahiko. Hula kahiko is not only the dance, kahiko entails meaningful chants, gathering plants (kinolau), and the creation of lei. Please join us as we share our culture through chants that are significant for gathering. Learn to dance a hula kahiko, and learn about the creation of our kupe`e (bracelets).

name: GRAND OPERA SEASON
description:
HOT launches the 2011 Grand Opera Season with its devilish production of Faust by Charles Gounod.  Directed by HOT's General and Artistic Director Henry Akina, Faust showcases a seasoned cast to tell the story of Satan's grip on the human soul.  John Bellemar, last seen at HOT in the high tenor role of Don Ottavio and Almaviva, returns to the HOT stage in the title role. Soprano Melody Moore makes her HOT stage debut in the role of Marguerite.  She has been heard at many companies throughout the United States.  Bass Jamie Offenbach makes his debut in the role of Mephistopheles with this production. Mark Flint returns to HOT to conduct Faust.

The centerpiece of the season is Gaetano Donizetti's Lucia di Lammermoor.  HOT's Executive Director Karen Tiller stages a storybook cast for this dramatic tragedy set to powerful music.  It will be presented in Italian with English subtitles. Nancy Allen Lundy, takes the stage in the title role and partners with Jorge Lopez-Yanez as Lucia's lover Edgardo. Gregory Gerbrandt makes his HOT debut as Lucia’s manipulating evil brother Enrico.  Maestro Michael conducts this opera.  

The season finale, Giuseppe Verdi's unforgettable classic, La Traviata, also be staged by Henry Akina.  Maestro Ty Paterson takes the baton to conduct this audience favorite.  The celebrated Uruguayan soprano Luz del Alba appears as Violetta. Eric Margiore sings the tenor role of Alfredo. Star baritone Jake Gardner appears as the elder Germont.

Hear the award winning sounds of Ledward Kaapana and Mike Kaawa, along with the unique voice of Kamakakehau Fernandez, an award winning falsetto entertainer. Kamakakehau brings a Hawaiian operatic style to his music. No charge.

name: HAWAII OPERA THEATRE - LA TRAVIATA
description:
Hawaii Opera Theatre's season finale, Giuseppe Verdi's unforgettable classic, La Traviata, will be staged by Henry Akina February 25, 27 & Mar 1 at the Blaisdell Concert Hall. Maestro Ty Paterson takes the baton to conduct this audience favorite. The celebrated Uruguayan soprano Luz del Alba appears as Violetta. She has made her mark on many companies in the United States and abroad, most recently touring with the Venice Opera. She recently appeared in the Republic of China as Violetta and was last heard at HOT in the role of Donna Anna in Don Giovanni. Eric Margiore sings the tenor role of Alfredo. "He is an ideal match vocally and in personality for the role opposite Luz del Alba," Akina said. In demand across the U.S. and in Europe for his great acting and singing abilities, Margiore makes his debut at HOT in this role after having auditioned for the company in New York. Star baritone Jake Gardner appears as the elder Germont, a role often thought to be based on the father of Alexandre Dumas who wrote the novel upon which La Traviata is based. Jake made his debut at HOT in Il Trittico and continued that season to sing Scarpia in Tosca. Last season, Gardner was heard in the role of Wotan in HOT's premiere of Die Walküre. La Traviata will be presented in Italian with English subtitles.

name: PRINCE KUHIO CELEBRATION - COMMEMORATIVE CEREMONIES
description: As part of the Prince Kuhio Celebration and in honor of his birthday, come observe the Native Hawaiian protocol of honoring Prince Kuhio through giving hookupu (offerings, gifts) and through dance and singing. Join us on the day of Prince Kuhio's birth near the location where he was born to honor his achievements and his importance to the people of Hawaii. Open to the public at no charge. These commemorative ceremonies are sponsored by the Royal Order of Kamehameha.

description: The Wiki Wiki One Day Vintage Collectibles & Hawaiiana Show is a strictly vintage 20 years and older show and sale at the Blaisdell Center Hawaii Suites in Honolulu. Vendors are from Mainland U.S., Outer Islands and Oahu with everything from Aloha shirts, antiques, art, estate jewelry, dolls, furniture, asian antiques, fine glassware, Hawaiiana, coins, stamps, kitchenware, koa, surf items, ukulele and more! The three annual Wiki Wiki shows are in Spring, October and December. They're a 91 table show with no presales to the vendors until early entry at 9 am.

description:
KAHULUI – Maui Pops Orchestra will welcome the Pocket Opera Company of San Francisco to the Maui Arts & Cultural Center’s Castle Theater Sunday, March 13, at 3:30 p.m. for a performance of “Elixir of Love” by Donizetti. The San Francisco Pocket Opera is known for its English translations of famous operas.

The translations are the work of opera founder and artistic director Donald Pippin, who moved to San Francisco in 1952 and has been part of the city’s music scene ever since.  Pippin’s 80-plus translations are witty and charming, making opera accessible to listeners who otherwise might find the idea of this classic art form a bit stuffy. “Pippin is to opera what Mark Twain was to American literature, a breath of fresh air and a national treasure,” according to the Sacramento Bee.

Pippin himself will be on hand at the Maui concert to present narratives setting up the various scenes performed by several lead singers from San Francisco. The chorus will be made up of local performers, while Maui Pops provides orchestral accompaniment. In addition to “Elixir of Love,” the orchestra will perform music from famous operas, including the Overture to “Die Meistersinger” by Wagner.

Tickets are $15, $35 and $45, plus a $3 facility fee. Call the MACC box office at 242-7469 or purchase online at www.mauiarts.org.

name: FROM BABYLON TO BATHS LECTURE
description:
Dr. Jonathan M. Bloom examines the history of tile decoration in the Islamic lands, beginning with pre-Islamic antecedents and continuing to modern times, when mathematicians and artists were exploring the theoretical bases and aesthetic possibilities of Islamic geometric designs. Jonathan M. Bloom shares the Professorship of Islamic and Asian Art at Boston College and the Chair of Islamic Art at Virginia Commonwealth University with his wife, scholar Sheila Blair. His most recent book is Arts of the City Victorious: the Art and Architecture of the Fatimids in North Africa and Egypt (2007). Together with his wife, Bloom edited the Grove Encyclopedia of Islamic Art and Architecture (2009) and Rivers of Paradise: Water in Islamic Art and Culture (2009), and served as consultants to the documentary Islam: Empire of Faith, which aired on PBS.

Honolulu Symphony Musicians present
A Chamber Music Concert with Pianist Helen Huang

Schubert’s Trout Quintet and other favorites are featured in this afternoon of stellar ensemble players. Internationally acclaimed pianist Helen Huang, who won the New York Philharmonic's Young People's Competition at age 16, returns once again to perform with some of our best local musicians. Joining her are soprano Kristin Stone; Ignace “Iggy” Jang, violin; Ethan Pernela, viola; Joanna Morrison-Pernela, cello; Geoffrey Stone, bass; and Norman F. Foster, clarinet. They present Brahms' Clarinet Trio and three Schubert works—The Shepherd on the Rock, the well-known song Die Forelle (The Trout), and his popular quintet dubbed “The Trout” after the song that inspired the theme and variations movement. Huang appears with top orchestras around the world, but her love of fine chamber music continues to lead her back to the Doris Duke Theatre. This is her third concert here in support of the Honolulu Symphony Musicians.

name: A RARE PAIR OF IMPERIAL KOREAN SCREENS FROM THE HONOLULU ACADEMY OF ARTS PERMANENT COLLECTION
description:
On opening day, one of the Academy’s galleries was called the “Korean Room,” and may have been the earliest gallery dedicated to Korean art in the United States. Among the Academy’s most important early Korean art acquisitions was a monumental pair of imperial Korean screens depicting cranes and other auspicious symbols of longevity. Due to their fragile condition, the museum was unable to place these screens on public display for several decades.

Thanks to a grant from the National Research Institute of Cultural Heritage (NRICH), a Korean government agency, these screens were conserved in 2006, after which they were displayed in Seoul’s National Museum of Korea as the focus of a special exhibition. The Academy unveiled the freshened screens in 2009 and will once again display them in 2011, to coincide with the annual conference of the Association of Asian Studies, the country’s leading scholarly organization dedicated to Asia, in Honolulu. In addition, on view will be Korean ceramics that were also conserved with an NRICH grant.

venue: In Waikiki on the Honolulu Zoo fence, Monsarrat Avenue, across the street from Kapiolani Bandstand
description: Every Sat & Sun: for over 50 years Art On The Zoo Fence has been one of Hawaii’s lasting treasures, enriching the public's experience by providing the opportunity to freely view and enjoy artwork and to meet Hawaii's artists in person. Artists participating in Art On The Zoo Fence also comprise and contribute to a non profit group called Zoo Fence Artists, which contributes annually to various organizations to promote arts education for children. Every Saturday and Sunday year round, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Art On The Zoo Fence artists present their artwork for viewing and sale in Waikiki along the Honolulu Zoo fence on Monsarrat Avenue, across from the bandstand at Kapiolani Park.
